verdict_reason: EnMAP (30km swath, tasked, registration+proposal via planning.enmap.org) and PRISMA (registration portal gave an unresolvable redirect loop, unverifiable) are opportunistic missions. Neither exposes an archive-coverage tool confirming existing EU arable-land scenes inside a growing season. Coverage is too sparse/unconfirmed to promise an auditable scene set in 8 months.

ground_truth.construction_protocol: Self-referential: co-locate an EnMAP/PRISMA scene near-date with a Sentinel-2 scene over EuroCrops/LPIS arable parcels; derive soil-line/red-edge hyperspectral indices per pixel and compare to the S2-derived N-prescription zone to flag divergence.
ground_truth.label_count_estimate: No discrete labels; pixel-level comparison limited to however many EnMAP/PRISMA scenes actually coincide with target parcels and a growing-season window (unconfirmed, likely small).

compute_path.platform: Local (MacBook, no GPU) using EnMAP/PRISMA L2A reflectance + Sentinel-2 L2A, index math and linear spectral unmixing in Python (rasterio/numpy)
compute_path.why: No model training required, only per-pixel index/unmixing arithmetic on downloaded scenes; CPU-only, fits C9's no-sustained-GPU rule.

notes: PRISMA's registration pages (prisma.asi.it/missionselect, prismauserregistration.asi.it) could not be fetched: a genuine http/https redirect loop and a TLS cert error. EnMAP's planning.enmap.org (tasking + archive browse) also failed on TLS cert error, so archive coverage over any specific EU arable AOI could not be confirmed for either mission. Both are narrow-swath (~30km), tasked/opportunistic sensors, unlike systematic Sentinel-2 — the core unresolved feasibility risk here.
